summary: An EatingWell article by Carolyn Malcoun (published April 13, 2022) explaining that banana peels are edible and can be eaten raw, cooked or frozen. It covers their fiber content, the need to wash peels and the pesticide residue concern, digestive precautions, the environmental benefit of reducing food waste, and examples of culinary and non-food uses. The article is a clipped web page, and its navigation, related-article links and footer were ignored.
one_line: EatingWell article explaining that banana peels are edible, their fiber and pesticide considerations, food-waste benefits, and ways to cook with them.
key_facts: Carolyn Malcoun wrote the EatingWell article 'Can You Eat Banana Peels?', published April 13, 2022.
Research published in Process Safety and Environmental Protection found banana peels are 71% to 83% fiber.
The EatingWell recipe-analysis database does not have nutrition information for banana peels.
The Environmental Working Group says banana cultivation is pesticide-intensive, and residues could be on the peels.
The article advises scrubbing banana peels under running water before eating them and considering organic bananas.
The peel makes up 30% to 40% of the banana, and humans discard approximately 3.5 million tons of banana peels every year.
Discarded food is the biggest type of garbage in landfills, where it emits methane and other greenhouse gases.
High fiber in banana peels can cause digestive discomfort if a person starts eating lots right away, so the article advises starting slowly and drinking water.
For smoothies, the article suggests slicing unpeeled bananas before freezing and adding them straight from the freezer to the blender.
For banana bread or cake, unpeeled bananas can be frozen whole, trimmed of the blossom end and stem tip, thawed, pureed and stirred into the batter.

Nadiya Hussain, host of Nadiya's Time to Eat on Netflix and season 6 winner of The Great British Baking Show, said in an email that she eats banana peel with fermented fish and prawns or cooks it like pulled chicken.
Vegans use banana peels to make plant-based bacon, Bolognese sauce and pulled 'pork'.
A company called Banana Business in the Netherlands sells banana-peel 'pulled pork'.
Researchers are experimenting with banana-peel flour as a gluten-free alternative for breads and noodles.
Circular Systems created a fiber called Agriloop made from various crops including banana peels.
